headline: ML frameworks infer cell, tissue, and repertoire states from omics and imaging data
label: Machine Learning Omics Frameworks
summary: Recent work pairs graph transfer learning, foundation-model attributions, and explainable ML with spatial, single-cell, and repertoire data.
synthesis: The shared thread is machine learning frameworks that infer interpretable biological states from high-dimensional omics and imaging data, with quantitative validation. Spatial-DC deconvolves spatial proteomics spots into cell-type-resolved profiles via graph-enhanced transfer learning, SuperSCC hierarchically clusters scRNA-seq across more than 90 datasets, and MIAAIM aligns histology, imaging mass cytometry, and mass spectrometry imaging. SIGnature scores gene importance from attributions of single-cell foundation models, and an explainable pipeline links tumor macrophages to relapse in METABRIC and TCGA. What is new is breadth of scale and application: a pan-cancer spatial atlas of tertiary lymphoid structures across 12 cancers with H&E-based prediction of maturation, and a TCRβ-only transformer profiling MAIT- and iNKT-associated repertoire states in bulk data.
